item.title: U.S.-Caribbean Relations: The Cost of Postponing the 2025 Summit of the Americas
item.description: Americas Program Senior Associate Georges Fauriol and Mary Speck highlight the growing security challenges facing Caribbean nations, including the regional crises in Haiti and Venezuela, and propose a regional solution to the issues at hand.

item.title: The Manifest Modernization Act: Enhancing Visibility Into Forced Labor Risks in U.S. Supply Chains
item.description: By expanding access to customs manifests across all modes of transport, the Manifest Modernization Act hits on a large data blind spot in U.S. trade enforcement and supply chain transparency.

item.title: If You Don’t Eat Your Meat, You Can’t Have Any Pudding
item.description: This week, Bill Reinsch describes how Trump's use of leverage in trade negotiations differs from previous administrations.

item.title: Turning the AI Revolution into Dollar Dominance
item.description: Navin Girishankar argues that President Trump's Gulf chip deals enable billions in AI exports but miss what ensures dollar dominance. A compute-dollar successor to the petrodollar will keep China’s offer of AI plus digital yuan settlement in the rearview mirror.

item.title: Previewing India's AI Impact Summit with MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan
item.description: CSIS hosted S. Krishnan, Secretary of India’s Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, to outline India’s policy priorities and share insights into the goals and global aspirations shaping the upcoming AI Impact Summit.

item.title: Escalating Japan-China Tensions: Insights from the Past and Prospects for the Future
item.description: Bonny Lin and Kristi Govella analyze the recent escalation in tensions between Tokyo and Beijing over remarks made by Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi regarding Japan's response to a Taiwan contingency.

item.title: Assessing the Current Peace Deal for Ukraine: Opportunity or Strategic Trap?
item.description: Amid negotiations to end Russia’s war on Ukraine, the West must ensure that any agreed-upon peace deal includes Ukraine and provides it with security guarantees that prevent Russia from attacking in the future. Without them, Europe's security at large will be compromised.

item.title: The National Security Strategy: The Good, the Not So Great, and the Alarm Bells
item.description: This NSS marks an ideological and substantive shift in U.S. foreign policy, as the administration defines a new “America First” foreign policy doctrine that is deeply pragmatic, and perhaps short-sighted. This is a truly pivotal moment in the way the world works.

item.title: Putting the Industrial Base on a Wartime Footing
item.description: Putting the industrial base on a wartime footing will require strong leadership and consistent funding, with an investment in readiness for day one of any conflict, and the ability to maintain, repair, and replace the capabilities needed to prevail in any future fight.
